pumac-2012-finals-b-01.prompt: Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime. A prime $p$ is said to be *orange* if for every integer $a$ there exists an integer $r$ such that $r^q\equiv a\pmod p$. Prove that there are infinitely many orange primes.
pumac-2012-finals-b-01.answer: Every prime $p\not\equiv1\pmod q$ is orange (then $\gcd(p-1,q)=1$), and there are infinitely many such primes (Euclid-style argument with $N=qp_1\cdots p_k-1$).

pumac-2012-finals-b-02.prompt: Let $O_1,O_2,\dots,O_{2012}$ be $2012$ circles in the plane such that no circle intersects or contains any other circle and no two circles have the same radius. For each $1\le i<j\le2012$, let $P_{i,j}$ denote the point of intersection of the two external tangent lines to $O_i$ and $O_j$, and let $T$ be the set of all $P_{i,j}$ (so $|T|=\binom{2012}2=2023066$). Suppose there exists a subset $S\subset T$ with $|S|=2021056$ such that all points in $S$ lie on the same line. Prove that all points in $T$ lie on the same line.
pumac-2012-finals-b-02.answer: Monge's theorem: $P_{ab},P_{bc},P_{ac}$ are collinear. A graph on 2012 vertices with at least 2021056 edges is connected, and the collinearity makes adjacency transitive, so the graph is complete.
